The street grid is not drawn; the base map shows only the city outline, neighborhoods and suburbs. Bus alignments come from the CTA route shapefile at full detail. Where routes share a street, that stretch is drawn once; click it to list the routes, then pick one to see its whole path. Express routes (X routes, “Express” names and J14) follow their local streets and are marked EXP. Rail lines and stations come from CTA GIS files; line colours follow CTA’s official palette, so garage colours avoid those hues. Bus connections are stops within about 170 m of a station.

Bus lines are all drawn white, so garage colours appear only on markers, route chips and the panel. In Night Owl mode the map keeps only the Red and Blue rail lines. Which garage runs which route comes from chicagobus.org, which labels its lists as historical. CTA moves routes between garages from time to time, so check a current CTA notice before relying on one.

Night Owl routes are the ones with N-route service in the bus stop file. The map draws the daytime alignment.

Landmarks are placed by hand.

Chicago’s outline, the lakefront and the neighborhood shapes come from the blackmad/neighborhoods dataset (98 neighborhoods merged into one city shape), so they are close but not an official boundary. Suburb boundaries and names are Cook County’s official municipality file (simplified). The lake outside Chicago is still approximate. Stops marked temporarily out of service are left out.
